To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
6-OHDA lesions of adult rat SNC dopaminergic cells cause a slow, progressive loss of TH mRNA, whereas the protein levels are maintained for up to 1 year.
the loss of TH mRNA is a progressive, slow process, whereas the loss of TH protein is a fast process, and the slow and fast processes are not coupled.

6-OHDA lesions to the nigrostriatal dopaminergic pathway in adult rats cause a slow, progressive loss of mRNA for the TH enzyme, but not of TH protein, which is maintained by the striatal dopaminergc terminals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of TH gene expression in the adult brain, and the possible role of the protein turnover machinery in regulating TH gene expression.
understanding the mechanisms of slow neuron regression in adult brain, and we believe that the TH gene is a useful model to study the molecular biology and biochemistry of neuron aging.
understanding the mechanisms of slow changes in gene expression in dopamine neurons of the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the slow changes of TH gene expression in the SNC cell bodies after 6-OHDA lesions in rats are a model for neuron atrophy that is a normal process of aging in the adult mammalian brain.
the slow changes in gene expression of TH are a model of slow neuron regression in aging.

the loss of TH mRNA and the shrinkage of SNC neurons in the rat brain are two independent processes, and the loss of TH protein from the striatum is due to the loss of TH gene expression in SNC cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TH mRNA/cell is a more dynamic and sensitive indicator of neuron health than the TH protein.
the TH protein is maintained by the SNC neurons for a long period after the loss of their axonal targets.
a PEST motif is present in the TH protein of all vertebrates examined, including the rat and human, and that the PEST motif may be a point of control in slow neuron regression in the SNC of rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
slow changes in gene expression in neurons can occur without a change in cell size, and the loss of mRNA can precede cell body shrinkage.
slow changes of TH mRNA/cells in the SNC are a model for neuron atrophy that can be applied in aging research.
slow neuron regression can be studied in adult rats by 6-OHDA lesioning of the nigrostriatal system, and this model has the potential to reveal new information about the aging process.
